meta.purpose: Mock dataset for the Due Diligence design and prototype: project Cottonwood, following QA's data model (qa-data.json, extracted 2026-11-24).
meta.source: qa-data.json (QA build 0.1.0-alpha.78). Layer metadata (source agency, loaded date, update frequency, source line, coverage) is copied verbatim from QA; per-layer results are mock values for a site in Sacramento County.
conventions: name / theme fields are Title Case display labels; qaName / qaTheme keep QA's sentence-case strings. Units stay lowercase.
Ring quantities are per ring (donut), not cumulative. Status is the first ring with featureCount > 0.
Cells, findings, short text and distances use QA's formulas (statusRules below). Every count in this file is computed, not typed.
Feature names, parcel APNs, deep dive findings and the failure message are illustrative, not real records.
assumptions: No Data Yet = the four layers QA has never loaded for any county (isLoadable false, 0 features): Wildfire Hazard Potential 2023, Soil Map Units, Farmland Classification, Cropland Data Layer 2025. Sole Source Aquifers and US Landslide Inventory are loaded but have 0 Sacramento features, so they read Not Found, as QA does for Umatilla.
Not Applicable = none: both California-only layers (Legal Delta Boundary, CARB Air Districts) have Sacramento features. The NA state is on Hermiston Solar (QA project 4 data).

Brief flavor mapped to QA layers: Flood Zones 13% AE -> FEMA Flood Hazard Zones class mix (the layer covers 100% because Zone X counts); Zoning 80% AG-80 and Plan 70% Agriculture -> class shares on 100%-covered layers; Protected Lands -> PAD-US 4.1; National Highway System -> Primary Roads; Fire Hazard Severity Zones -> dropped (Wildfire Hazard Potential is No Data); Past Fire Perimeters -> Interagency Fire Perimeter History; County Parcels -> project Parcels (4), not a layer.
Ring areas use QA's buffer geometry approximated as area + perimeter x d + pi x d^2 with a 3.2 mi perimeter.

statusRules.rule: project4.layers[].project4.status values: on_site, within_ring_1 (0 to 1/4 mi), within_ring_2 (1/4 to 1 mi), within_ring_3 (1 to 5 mi), not_found, no_data_for_county, not_applicable. The app's internal state key is the first ring index with FeatureCount > 0, or 'none' / 'nodata' / 'na'. A layer's status is decided by FeatureCount per ring, not quantity. Ring quantities are per ring (donut), not cumulative.
statusRules.noDataRule: no_data_for_county when the layer has no completed load for the county; a loaded layer with 0 features in the rings is not_found.
statusRules.notApplicableRule: not_applicable when coveredStates excludes the project's state; finding "Covers <states> only".
statusRules.cellFormat: blank when featureCount = 0; >= 100 integer with commas; 10 to 100 one decimal; < 10 two decimals; trailing zeros trimmed; + " ac" / " mi"; points are a bare count.
statusRules.distanceFormat: <0.1 mi: 2 decimals, else 1 decimal, 0 = 'on the site'
statusRules.onSiteFinding: polygon: "<qty>, <pct> of the site[, mostly <top on-site class>]"; line: "<qty> on the site[, mostly <class>]"; "mostly" only when the layer has 2+ classes; first letter lowercased unless the class starts with a code. pct rounds to whole %, "under 1%" below 0.5%.
statusRules.noDataFinding: No data for this county yet

finalReport.title: Critical Issues Assessment: Cottonwood

sections.title: Letter
body: Re: Critical Issues Assessment for Cottonwood, 359 acres, Sacramento County, CA

ESA screened the Cottonwood site and the land within 5 miles of its boundary against 29 environmental and land use datasets on November 24, 2026. 25 had data for Sacramento County. Four (Wildfire Hazard Potential 2023, Soil Map Units, Farmland Classification and Cropland Data Layer 2025) are not yet loaded for the county and are not reflected here.

12 of the 25 screened datasets intersect the site. The constraints most likely to affect layout, schedule or entitlement are the agricultural general plan and zoning designations, the regulated floodplain and aquatic features on the site, the two transmission lines that cross it, and the Severe 15 ozone nonattainment classification, which bears on permitting for standby generators.

None of the screened datasets on their own point to a fatal flaw. Several findings rest on regional mapping and need field or records verification before they are relied on. Table 1 summarizes the findings by topic; the critical issues and recommended next steps follow.

topics.setting: Electric power transmission lines cross the site for 0.3 mi, one in the 220 to 287 kV class and one in the 100 to 161 kV class. State Route 99 is 0.3 mi from the boundary and the Union Pacific main line 0.9 mi. The nearest aviation facilities are a heliport at 4.3 mi and Franklin Field at 4.8 mi.
topics.recommendations: Confirm the owners, voltages and easement widths of both lines from title and the utility, and fit the building envelope to them. Ask the utility early about a large-load service study.

topics.setting: National Wetlands Inventory mapping shows 14.4 ac of wetlands on the site (4% of site), mostly freshwater emergent. NHDPlus HR flowlines run 1.6 mi across the site, including Deer Creek. No Wild and Scenic River or sole source aquifer lies within 5 mi.
topics.recommendations: Commission an aquatic resources delineation. If fill of wetlands or channels cannot be avoided, plan for Clean Water Act Section 404 and 401 permits and a California Fish and Game Code Section 1602 agreement.

topics.setting: The general plan designates 70% of the site Agricultural Cropland, 18% Agricultural-Residential and 12% Resource Conservation Area. Zoning is 80% AG-80 and 20% AR-10.
topics.recommendations: A data center is not an expected use under these designations. Hold a pre-application meeting with Sacramento County Planning to confirm the path, likely a General Plan Amendment and rezone with full CEQA review.

topics.setting: FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area covers 46.7 ac (13%) of the site: 41.6 ac Zone AE and 5.1 ac Zone A. The rest is Zone X. The site sits in seismic intensity MMI VI. The nearest past fire perimeter is 0.6 mi away; no Quaternary fault or mapped landslide lies within 5 mi.
topics.recommendations: Keep structures and critical equipment out of Zones AE and A, or plan for county floodplain permits and a FEMA map revision if the site is filled.

topics.setting: Current ranges of five federally listed species and one candidate overlap the site. The nearest designated critical habitat, for vernal pool tadpole shrimp, is 0.9 mi away.
topics.recommendations: Have a biologist assess habitat on site, with attention to the wetlands and Deer Creek corridor, and scope protocol surveys from that assessment.

topics.setting: Soils, farmland classification and cropland data are not yet loaded for Sacramento County.
topics.recommendations: Check Important Farmland mapping and Williamson Act status by hand before the land use strategy is set.

topics.setting: The nearest protected land in PAD-US is 0.2 mi from the boundary. The Legal Delta boundary is 3.8 mi away.
topics.recommendations: No action beyond confirming that no easement in PAD-US extends onto the site.

topics.setting: No National Register property is on the site; the nearest is 0.8 mi away. The National Register is a reference list and does not satisfy Section 106 or CEQA review.
topics.recommendations: Order a records search from the North Central Information Center and plan a pedestrian survey.

topics.setting: The site is in the Sacramento Metropolitan AQMD and inside the Sacramento Metro ozone nonattainment area, classified Severe 15.
topics.recommendations: Scope air permits for standby generators early. Emission offsets and limits on testing hours may apply and can shape generator count and fuel.

topics.setting: No Superfund NPL site lies within 5 mi.
topics.recommendations: A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment remains standard before acquisition.

topics.setting: The site lies in Census Tracts 94.05 and 94.06.
topics.recommendations: Review the tracts' Social Vulnerability Index values before community outreach is planned.

issues.body: Agricultural general plan and zoning designations cover the whole site. A data center will likely need a General Plan Amendment and rezone, a discretionary process with full CEQA review. This sets the schedule more than any physical constraint.
issues.action: Pre-application meeting with Sacramento County Planning before the purchase option deadline.

issues.body: 46.7 acres (13%) of the site is in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area, mostly Zone AE.
issues.action: Survey base flood elevations and lay out buildings outside Zones AE and A.

issues.body: 14.4 acres of mapped wetlands and 1.6 miles of streams, including Deer Creek, are on the site. Fill would trigger federal and state permits with long lead times.
issues.action: Aquatic resources delineation, then a site plan that avoids them.

issues.body: Two lines cross the site. Their easements limit the buildable area; the 230 kV line may also be the interconnection path.
issues.action: Title review of easements and an early load study request to the utility.

issues.body: The Severe 15 ozone classification raises the bar for permitting standby generators at the scale a data center needs.
issues.action: Air permit scoping with the Sacramento Metropolitan AQMD.

handoff.instructions: Look past the screened layers for anything that could stop or delay a data center here: moratoria, utility capacity, recent planning items, water supply, farmland contracts.

findings.finding: No moratorium on data centers or large electric loads found in Board of Supervisors or Planning Commission agendas from December 2025 to November 2026.

Sacramento County Planning Commission agendas, Dec 2025 to Nov 2026

findings.finding: The local utility sends new loads over 10 MW to a facility study and publishes no capacity figure for the substations nearest the site. A 300 MW campus would need transmission-level service.

sources.title: Utility integrated resource plan, load growth chapter

findings.finding: In October 2026 the Planning Commission continued a hearing on an agricultural-to-industrial rezone for a 140-acre site about 4 mi north of Cottonwood after neighbors raised traffic and farmland concerns.
The site overlies the South American Subbasin, which DWR ranks high priority. New groundwater use for cooling would fall under the subbasin's groundwater sustainability plan.
